title: Titans
summary: Titans are powerful, ancient beings that were summoned from the Spirit World of Huntik and then sealed away in Amulets by Lord Casterwill centuries ago. His personal Titans, the powerful Legendary Titans, were sealed within rings. Strong Seekers are able to invoke Titans from their Amulets. Titans, by nature, are neutral beings, although they tend to have the personality of their Seekers impressed upon them and may be unwilling to bond with Seekers whose personalities differ greatly from a previous owner. Titans do not think as humans do because they are spirit entities that rely more on their instincts. Although it is unnatural for Titans, bonded Seekers are able to communicate strategies to them.

sections.heading: History
sections.wikitext:
Titans are incredible warriors that were locked away inside Amulets after being summoned by [[Lord Casterwill]] from Huntik to aid in an ancient battle against the unimaginable evil force of the [[Nullifiers]] that threatened to destroy the world. The power of Titans has led to many of the world's myths and legends, in addition to those started to describe the original war. As history progressed, these Amulets fell into the hands of many Seekers around the world, including historical figures. 
[[File:S1E12 Dragons teeth Hoplite.jpg|thumb|[[Hoplite]] Amulets are recovered by [[Zhalia Moon]] from a chest hidden in the [[Argo]]]]
Many Amulets ended up in landmarks, monuments, tombs, and other varied locations, hidden for thousands of years until a "new age" of Seekers started gathering them and bonding with Titans. This can be traced back to the 20th century, around the time both [[the Organization]] and the [[Huntik Foundation]] were created and started forming a collection of Amulets to aid in acheiving their respective goals and fight each other whenever necessary. Other groups such as the [[Casterwill family]], [[Blood Spiral]], [[Guardians of Thor]] and many others have also used Titans for the same reasons. This new age of Seekers has brought some dormant Titans to life, such is the case with [[Gar-Ghoul]], in [[Rouen, France]]. {{Source|Into the River of Secrets}}

A lot of powerful and influential historical figures were [[Seekers]] and had used Titans, which in some cases help to explain some aspects of their notability and historical significancy. Such is the case with [[Joan of Arc]], who had visions of the future because of [[Arc|Arc, the Legendary Titan of Fate]]; or [[Vlad Dracul]], whose notoriety as an evil and monstrous human was reflected in his his bond with the Titan [[Antedeluvian]].

sections.heading: The Bond
sections.text:
bonds with Megataur]]
A Titan will most easily bond with Seekers whose personality is similar to its previous Seeker, and Titans which have not been bonded with any Seekers for a long time may prove difficult to bond. Also, if the new Seeker's personality is completely opposite to the Titan's previous Seeker, it may outright refuse to bond; this effect is amplified if the old Seeker of a Titan has been bonded with them for a long time. This made Dante Vale think DeFoe's Amulets were useless to the Huntik Foundation due to his intense personality and long-time use of his Titans, despite the use of Sorrowbond; however, Zhalia Moon was actually able to bond with his Gar-Ghoul, possibly because of her personality having a dark side. [The Mission]
 about to land safely due to the effects of bonding with Kipperin]]
The process of bonding with a Titan generally begins when someone touches an Amulet of that Titan; if the bond is successful, then the Amulet and the person may start emitting a glowing aura. Sometimes, just the process of bonding with a Titan can make that person know the Titan's name, even if they have never heard it before. [The Unseen Guide] [Den vs Harrison] This process can become more intense if it is the first time someone bonds with a Titan, like when Lok Lambert bonded with Kipperin, which occasionally made him levitate and prevent falls by just having its Amulet near him [A Seeker Is Born]. When Lok bonded with Freelancer, he was also shown brief glimpses of the future where he later uses the Titan. [The Casterwill Connection]

Titans may unbond with their Seeker if the Seeker's personality changes dramatically. A Titan will also unbond if its Seeker dies, although this may cause the Titan to go mad, as was the case with Madea or if their Amulet is lost for a long time [Ask Guggenheim]. However, Titans such as Fenris and Antedeluvian have been known to stay invoked and protect the Seeker's secrets. 
 loses control of Overlos as Archwarder's ability targets the Amulet of Will]]
A spell known as Sorrowbond is capable of unnaturally severing the bond between Seeker and Titan and thus allowing another Seeker to attempt to bond with them. The affects of this spell, however, are overcome once the original Seeker touches the Titan's Amulet again. Titans themselves also have abilities that could interfere with the Seeker-Titan bond. Archwarder, for example, can make powerful Titans hard to control or invoke; while Dendras can control enemy Titans, turning them against their Seekers and making them follow orders from Dendras' Seeker instead. Araknos' webs can also control the actions of other Titans, rendering them useless or making ally Titans fight each other. [The Secret of Two Generations] Dominator's spikes can make a Titan unpredictable and agitated, refusing to follow their Seeker's orders. [The Mission] Demigorgan, the Legendary Titan of Betrayal, can also create Seeker and Titan mimics to subvert the bond and confuse both, hypnotizing them into thinking the mimics are real. [Dante's Return] 

Titans can, in a way, remember past Seekers despite being currently bonded with another one. For example, Pendragon reacted to the Demigorgan mimic of the first Champion of Casterwill despite being currently powerbonded with Lok Lambert. [Dante's Return]

sections.heading: Summoning
sections.text:
summons his signature Titan, Venadek]]
When a Titan is not invoked, it resides in the Spirit World. A Seeker can then invoke it by holding their Amulet and calling out their name, with a few exceptions. Usually, a Titan is summoned only after the Seeker has bonded with it, but this is not always the case, resulting in the summoned Titan simply not following the person's orders. [Memory Lane] An exception to this is when Lord Casterwill's spirit is present to help summon the Titan, in which case it will follow the Seeker's as if they were bonded. [Knight of the Willblade]
 collapses after invoking Caliban, Metagolem and Behemoth within a few minutes]]
Summoning a Titan, and keeping it summoned, is a process that requires willpower, [The Casterwill Connection] physical stamina and focus. As such, if one summons too many Titans, they make runout of willpower to summon any more or cast spells [The Divine Comedy]. Similarly, they may also get physically tired and even pass out, depending on the strength of the Titans invoked and the interval between each summoning. [To Be Together] [Coming of Age] However, this exhaustion can be trained to be less significant over time. For example, the first time Zhalia Moon invoked King Basilisk, she almost passed out [Absent Heroes], but later on she was able to invoke it as well as many other Titans without issue. [The Divine Comedy] If a Seeker fails to concentrate when a Titan is invoked, it may transform into a glowing essence which will then return to its Amulet, such as when Den Fears' first Titan, Vigilante, returned to its Amulet after Den was punched. [Den vs Harrison] Something similar happened when Lok Lambert was hit by a Poisonfang spell, causing his Powerbonded Baselaird to fall to its knees. [The Tower of Nostradamus]

A Titan will also return to its Amulet if it has taken too much physical damage, or if its Seekers orders it to do so. When a Titan is taken out the first way, its Seeker may feel discomfort and even pain, incapacitating them briefly and generally exhausting them; [Dante's Return] the Titan will then be unable to be summoned again for an extended period of time, with only the spell Newlife being able to circumvent this. [The Divine Comedy][The Mission] When a Titan is sent back to its Amulet the second way, however, it can be re-summoned at the Seeker's will. [The Spiral Mark][Rassimov's Secret]

sections.heading: Destruction and Banishment
sections.text:
cries as Sabriel's Amulet fades into dust]]
While a Titan's spirit is usually immortal and returns safely to its Amulet when a standard battle is lost, there are rare instances where a Titan is permanently lost to its Seeker and its physical form is destroyed. Titans can be entirely erased from existence through the use of dark magic or have their physical form permanently lost due to the destruction of their Amulet. In some cases, the spiritual energy of a Titan lives on and is permanently returned to the Spirit World, while in other cases, the Titan ceases to exist entirely. The destruction of an Amulet also causes great discomfort to the Titan's Seeker. [The Blood Spiral] [S2E21]

There are several unique ways for a Titan's physical form or Amulet to be destroyed, rendering them unable to be invoked:

*If a Seeker demands that a Titan does not return to its Amulet after taking too much damage, sustaining further consecutive blows will cause its Amulet to permanently disintegrate, destroying the Titan. [Dante's Return] Similarly, if a Titan refuses to follow orders or cannot return due to external forces —such as the mental hijacking effect of Dominator's spikes— it and its Amulet will be permanently destroyed after taking too many blows. [The Mission] 

*The spell Darkvoid acts as a black hole that can completely disintegrate anything beyond its event horizon in seconds. In the case of a Titan, it can be pulled in and erased, with their Amulets destroyed for good. [Memory Lane] 

*Legion, the Legendary Titan of War, can absorb individual Titans and cause their physical Amulets to disintegrate. When Legion's Amulet was later shattered by Lok Lambert using the Willblade, Legion was destroyed, and the spirits of all the Titans it had absorbed over the centuries were freed and permanently sent back to the Spirit World. [The Spiral Mark]

*Umbra represents a unique case of a Titan that suffers an unrecoverable drain on its energy whenever it teleports other living entities. [The Power of Umbra] Pushing this process past its definitive limit causes the Titan's spirit to permanently disintegrate away. [Dante's Return]

A Titan can also be permanently banished directly to the world of Huntik by the power of Overlos, the Titan of Immortality, who can create an open portal that links the human dimension to the native spirit realm, and can send Titans into it leaving their physical anchors behind. [The Mission]

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
In terms of appearance, Titans present in variety of forms, some of which can look like humans and certain animals. Generally, Titans do not talk, but do have the ability to make sounds such as grunting, groaning, screaming or other sounds depending for example on what animal they appear to relate to. They communicate with their Seekers telepathically. However, Titans are able to understand and follow their Seeker's orders. This communication becomes enhanced when a Titan becomes powerbonded, also allowing Seekers to communicate telepathically. 
 gestures at Dante to back out|180x180px]]
Titans also do not think the way humans do, but rather behave like animals in many ways and will follow their instincts and do as their Seekers orders. For example, Gareon regularly comforts its Seeker, Zhalia Moon, in a cat-like manner when she's feeling down. Cherit and Madea are notable known exceptions that can talk and even reason, the former can even play chess and acts nigh-identically to a human apart from the lack of physiological needs. Apart from these exceptions, some Titans are shown to display some level of critical thinking, such as when Ariel signaled Dante Vale to retreat after the ambush against Rassimov went south, or when Solwing tried to get Dante of the aforementioned situation by snatching the Necklace of Tutankhamun out of his hands and using it as bait for Rassimov. [Rassimov's Secret]

Some Titans do appear to have what resembles a personality or temperament; Lindorm, for example, requires its Seeker to be assertive and in control of their emotions, otherwise it will act aggressively and ignore orders. They're also shown to immediately feel threatened and distressed in the presence of Nullifiers, such as when Lilith the Queen and Powerbonded Caliban immediately stopped fighting each other when Void was invoked, looking to fight it instead. [The Spiral Mark] In contrast to this, Titans will immediately stop what they are doing to make a bow in the presence of Lord Casterwill's spirit. [Knight of the Willblade] Titans generally lack any physiological needs that biological living beings do, such as the need for food, sleep or oxygen (though Cherit still shows enjoyment in eating). [The Casterwill Client] [The Treasures of the Argonauts] [Back Home]

sections.text:
There are eight core Titan types in which the Titans are classified. In general, a Titan's type corresponds to the region and cultures whose myths the Titan influenced. Titan's type can generally be identified through the design of their Amulet as well the coloration of their energy essence. The Legendary Titans also each belong to one of the eight Titan types based on their mythological and cultural origins but the majority are contained in Rings. 

{| class="article-table" style="width:100%; text-align:left;"

These tend to be the basis for the legends of Medieval Europe and are commonly warrior-based Titans.

These tend to be the basis for Celtic legends and are commonly tied to an aspect of nature.

These tend to be the basis for Egyptian legends and are commonly themed around mummies and death. Most of these Titans are seen in the hands of evil Seekers.

These tend to be the basis for Greco-Roman mythologies and have a tendency to be warriors like their Draco-Titan brethren.

These tend to be the colossal Titans composed of rock or ice, forming the basis for golems found in European, Norse, and Greco-Roman legends.

These tend to be the basis for Native American legends of North and Central America and are often based upon spiritual powers and animals.

These tend to be the basis for African legends and are commonly based upon desert insects and arachnids. Like their Hecto-Titan brethren, most are seen in the hands of evil Seekers.

These tend to be the basis for legends throughout Asia, often inspired by Eastern fighting arts.

 The Legendary Titans represent the highest tier of Titans. Due to their immense power, they were among the first Titans brought to Earth by Lord Casterwill to fight the Nullifiers. Unlike other Titans, most Legendary Titans are sealed within Rings rather than standard Amulets.

sections.heading: Powerbonded Titans
sections.wikitext:
[[File:Caliban PB 2.jpg|thumb|160px|[[Caliban]] in his Powerbonded form]]
''Main Article: '''[[Powerbond]]'''''

A Titan with an exceptionally strong bond to its Seeker may become so closely synchronized as to form a [[Powerbond]]. In this state, the Titan undergoes a physical transformation, and becomes significantly more powerful both in attack and defense. Although Titans do not naturally think in human terms, [[Powerbond|Powerbonded]] Titans are able to communicate more directly with their Seekers through telepathy. 

While the most visible changes occur to the Titan itself, with Powerbonded Titans typically gaining golden armor, Seekers may also gain additional abilities through the Powerbond. An example of this is [[Dante Vale]] and [[Caliban|Caliban's]] "Mirror Fight" ability, in which the two perfectly mirror each other’s movements.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.wikitext:
*In early sketches and in the first trailer, Titans instead were called Essences. Also, their Amulets and summoning were totally different from now.
*A track is played during every Titan summoning sequence. Each faction of [[Seekers]] has a few different tracks associated to them.
**However, it doesn't only relate to the faction of the Seeker, but also if they are fighting for good or bad intentions, as exemplified by when a track usually used for evil Seekers is played when [[Zhalia Moon|Zhalia]] invokes [[King Basilisk]] to fight [[Sophie Casterwill|Sophie]] in "[[The Divine Comedy]]".

A Titan can also be permanently banished directly to the world of Huntik by the power of Overlos, the Titan of Immortality, who can create an open portal that links the human dimension to the native spirit realm, and can send Titans into it leaving their physical anchors behind. [The Mission] 

==Behavior==
In terms of appearance, Titans present in variety of forms, some of which can look like humans and certain animals. Generally, Titans do not talk, but do have the ability to make sounds such as grunting, groaning, screaming or other sounds depending for example on what animal they appear to relate to. They communicate with their Seekers telepathically. However, Titans are able to understand and follow their Seeker's orders. This communication becomes enhanced when a Titan becomes powerbonded, also allowing Seekers to communicate telepathically. 
 gestures at Dante to back out|180x180px]]
Titans also do not think the way humans do, but rather behave like animals in many ways and will follow their instincts and do as their Seekers orders. For example, Gareon regularly comforts its Seeker, Zhalia Moon, in a cat-like manner when she's feeling down. Cherit and Madea are notable known exceptions that can talk and even reason, the former can even play chess and acts nigh-identically to a human apart from the lack of physiological needs. Apart from these exceptions, some Titans are shown to display some level of critical thinking, such as when Ariel signaled Dante Vale to retreat after the ambush against Rassimov went south, or when Solwing tried to get Dante of the aforementioned situation by snatching the Necklace of Tutankhamun out of his hands and using it as bait for Rassimov. [Rassimov's Secret]

Some Titans do appear to have what resembles a personality or temperament; Lindorm, for example, requires its Seeker to be assertive and in control of their emotions, otherwise it will act aggressively and ignore orders. They're also shown to immediately feel threatened and distressed in the presence of Nullifiers, such as when Lilith the Queen and Powerbonded Caliban immediately stopped fighting each other when Void was invoked, looking to fight it instead. [The Spiral Mark] In contrast to this, Titans will immediately stop what they are doing to make a bow in the presence of Lord Casterwill's spirit. [Knight of the Willblade] Titans generally lack any physiological needs that biological living beings do, such as the need for food, sleep or oxygen (though Cherit still shows enjoyment in eating). [The Casterwill Client] [The Treasures of the Argonauts] [Back Home] 

==Types of Titans==
There are eight core Titan types in which the Titans are classified. In general, a Titan's type corresponds to the region and cultures whose myths the Titan influenced. Titan's type can generally be identified through the design of their Amulet as well the coloration of their energy essence. The Legendary Titans also each belong to one of the eight Titan types based on their mythological and cultural origins but the majority are contained in Rings.

==Powerbonded Titans==
 in his Powerbonded form]]
Main Article: Powerbond

A Titan with an exceptionally strong bond to its Seeker may become so closely synchronized as to form a Powerbond. In this state, the Titan undergoes a physical transformation, and becomes significantly more powerful both in attack and defense. Although Titans do not naturally think in human terms, Powerbonded Titans are able to communicate more directly with their Seekers through telepathy. 

While the most visible changes occur to the Titan itself, with Powerbonded Titans typically gaining golden armor, Seekers may also gain additional abilities through the Powerbond. An example of this is Dante Vale and Caliban's "Mirror Fight" ability, in which the two perfectly mirror each other’s movements.

==Trivia== 
*In early sketches and in the first trailer, Titans instead were called Essences. Also, their Amulets and summoning were totally different from now.
*A track is played during every Titan summoning sequence. Each faction of Seekers has a few different tracks associated to them.
**However, it doesn't only relate to the faction of the Seeker, but also if they are fighting for good or bad intentions, as exemplified by when a track usually used for evil Seekers is played when Zhalia invokes King Basilisk to fight Sophie in "The Divine Comedy".

[[Rings]] |type1 = {{Amulet|Draco}} [[Draco-Titans]] |type2 = {{Amulet|Litho}} [[Litho-Titans]] |type3 = {{Amulet|Gaia}} [[Gaia-Titans]] |type4 = {{Amulet|Meso}} [[Meso-Titans]] |type5 = {{Amulet|Hecto}} [[Hecto-Titans]] |type6 = {{Amulet|Swara}} [[Swara-Titans]] |type7 = {{Amulet|Krono}} [[Krono-Titans]] |type8 = {{Amulet|Yama}} [[Yama-Titans]] |type9 = [[Legendary Titans]]}} '''Titans''' are powerful, ancient beings that were summoned from the [[Spirit World]] of Huntik and then sealed away in [[Amulets]] by [[Lord Casterwill]] centuries ago. His personal Titans, the powerful [[Legendary Titans]], were sealed within [[rings]]. Strong [[Seekers]] are able to invoke Titans from their Amulets. Titans, by nature, are neutral beings, although they tend to have the personality of their Seekers impressed upon them and may be unwilling to bond with Seekers whose personalities differ greatly from a previous owner. {{source|Ask Guggenheim}} Titans do not think as humans do because they are spirit entities that rely more on their instincts. Although it is unnatural for Titans, bonded Seekers are able to communicate strategies to them. {{source|The Treasures of the Argonauts}} ==History== Titans are incredible warriors that were locked away inside Amulets after being summoned by [[Lord Casterwill]] from Huntik to aid in an ancient battle against the unimaginable evil force of the [[Nullifiers]] that threatened to destroy the world. The power of Titans has led to many of the world's myths and legends, in addition to those started to describe the original war. As history progressed, these Amulets fell into the hands of many Seekers around the world, including historical figures. [[File:S1E12 Dragons teeth Hoplite.jpg|thumb|[[Hoplite]] Amulets are recovered by [[Zhalia Moon]] from a chest hidden in the [[Argo]]]] Many Amulets ended up in landmarks, monuments, tombs, and other varied locations, hidden for thousands of years until a "new age" of Seekers started gathering them and bonding with Titans. This can be traced back to the 20th century, around the time both [[the Organization]] and the [[Huntik Foundation]] were created and started forming a collection of Amulets to aid in acheiving their respective goals and fight each other whenever necessary. Other groups such as the [[Casterwill family]], [[Blood Spiral]], [[Guardians of Thor]] and many others have also used Titans for the same reasons. This new age of Seekers has brought some dormant Titans to life, such is the case with [[Gar-Ghoul]], in [[Rouen, France]]. {{Source|Into the River of Secrets}} A lot of powerful and influential historical figures were [[Seekers]] and had used Titans, which in some cases help to explain some aspects of their notability and historical significancy. Such is the case with [[Joan of Arc]], who had visions of the future because of [[Arc|Arc, the Legendary Titan of Fate]]; or [[Vlad Dracul]], whose notoriety as an evil and monstrous human was reflected in his his bond with the Titan [[Antedeluvian]]. ==The Bond== [[File:S1E12 Grier Governor bond.jpg|thumb|[[Grier]] bonds with [[Megataur]]]] A Titan will most easily bond with Seekers whose personality is similar to its previous Seeker, and Titans which have not been bonded with any Seekers for a long time may prove difficult to bond. Also, if the new Seeker's personality is completely opposite to the Titan's previous Seeker, it may outright refuse to bond; this effect is amplified if the old Seeker of a Titan has been bonded with them for a long time. This made Dante Vale think [[DeFoe]]'s Amulets were useless to the [[Huntik Foundation]] due to his intense personality and long-time use of his Titans, despite the use of [[Sorrowbond]]; however, [[Zhalia Moon]] was actually able to bond with his [[Gar-Ghoul]], possibly because of her personality having a dark side. {{Source|The Mission}} [[File:S1E01 Lok flying bridge.png|thumb|[[Lok Lambert]] about to land safely due to the effects of bonding with [[Kipperin]]]] The process of bonding with a Titan generally begins when someone touches an Amulet of that Titan; if the bond is successful, then the Amulet and the person may start emitting a glowing aura. Sometimes, just the process of bonding with a Titan can make that person know the Titan's name, even if they have never heard it before. {{Source|The Unseen Guide}} {{Source|Den vs Harrison}} This process can become more intense if it is the first time someone bonds with a Titan, like when [[Lok Lambert]] bonded with [[Kipperin]], which occasionally made him levitate and prevent falls by just having its [[Amulets|Amulet]] near him {{Source|A Seeker Is Born}}. When Lok bonded with [[Freelancer]], he was also shown brief glimpses of the future where he later uses the Titan. {{Source|The Casterwill Connection}} Titans may unbond with their Seeker if the Seeker's personality changes dramatically.{{Sourceneeded}} A Titan will also unbond if its Seeker dies, although this may cause the Titan to go mad, as was the case with [[Madea]] or if their Amulet is lost for a long time {{source|Ask Guggenheim}}. However, Titans such as [[Fenris]] and [[Antedeluvian]] have been known to stay invoked and protect the Seeker's secrets. [[File:S1E26 Professor Amulet of Will.jpg|thumb|[[The Professor]] loses control of [[Overlos]] as [[Archwarder]]'s ability targets the [[Amulet of Will]]]] A spell known as [[Sorrowbond]] is capable of unnaturally severing the bond between Seeker and Titan and thus allowing another Seeker to attempt to bond with them. The affects of this spell, however, are overcome once the original Seeker touches the Titan's Amulet again. Titans themselves also have abilities that could interfere with the Seeker-Titan bond. [[Archwarder]], for example, can make powerful Titans hard to control or invoke; while [[Dendras]] can control enemy Titans, turning them against their Seekers and making them follow orders from Dendras' Seeker instead. [[Araknos]]' webs can also control the actions of other Titans, rendering them useless or making ally Titans fight each other. {{Source|The Secret of Two Generations}} [[Dominator]]'s spikes can make a Titan unpredictable and agitated, refusing to follow their Seeker's orders. {{Source|The Mission}} [[Demigorgan]], the Legendary Titan of Betrayal, can also create Seeker and Titan mimics to subvert the bond and confuse both, hypnotizing them into thinking the mimics are real. {{Source|Dante's Return}} Titans can, in a way, remember past Seekers despite being currently bonded with another one. For example, [[Pendragon]] reacted to the Demigorgan mimic of the [[Champion of Casterwill|first Champion of Casterwill]] despite being currently [[Powerbond|powerbonded]] with [[Lok Lambert]]. {{Source|Dante's Return}} == Summoning == [[File:S1E23 Tersly summons Venadek.jpg|thumb|180x180px|[[Tersly]] summons his signature Titan, [[Venadek]]]] When a Titan is not invoked, it resides in the [[Spirit World]]. A Seeker can then invoke it by holding their Amulet and calling out their name, with a few exceptions. Usually, a Titan is summoned only after the Seeker has bonded with it, but this is not always the case, resulting in the summoned Titan simply not following the person's orders. {{Source|Memory Lane}} An exception to this is when [[Lord Casterwill]]'s spirit is present to help summon the Titan, in which case it will follow the Seeker's as if they were bonded. {{Source|Knight of the Willblade}} [[File:S1E21 Dante collapasing Lok.png|thumb|[[Dante Vale]] collapses after invoking [[Caliban]], [[Metagolem]] and [[Behemoth]] within a few minutes]] Summoning a Titan, and keeping it summoned, is a process that requires willpower, {{Source|The Casterwill Connection}} physical stamina and focus. As such, if one summons too many Titans, they make runout of willpower to summon any more or cast spells {{Source|The Divine Comedy}}. Similarly, they may also get physically tired and even pass out, depending on the strength of the Titans invoked and the interval between each summoning. {{Source|To Be Together}} {{Source|Coming of Age}} However, this exhaustion can be trained to be less significant over time. For example, the first time [[Zhalia Moon]] invoked [[King Basilisk]], she almost passed out {{Source|Absent Heroes}}, but later on she was able to invoke it as well as many other Titans without issue. {{Source|The Divine Comedy}} If a Seeker fails to concentrate when a Titan is invoked, it may transform into a glowing essence which will then return to its Amulet, such as when [[Den Fears]]' first Titan, [[Vigilante]], returned to its Amulet after Den was punched. {{Source|Den vs Harrison}} Something similar happened when [[Lok Lambert]] was hit by a [[Poisonfang]] spell, causing his [[Baselaird|Powerbonded Baselaird]] to fall to its knees. {{Source|The Tower of Nostradamus}} A Titan will also return to its Amulet if it has taken too much physical damage, or if its Seekers orders it to do so. When a Titan is taken out the first way, its Seeker may feel discomfort and even pain, incapacitating them briefly and generally exhausting them; {{Source|Dante's Return}} the Titan will then be unable to be summoned again for an extended period of time, with only the spell [[Newlife]] being able to circumvent this. {{Source|The Divine Comedy}}{{Source|The Mission}} When a Titan is sent back to its Amulet the second way, however, it can be re-summoned at the Seeker's will. {{Source|The Spiral Mark}}{{Source|Rassimov's Secret}} == Destruction and Banishment == [[File:S1E26 Sophie Sabriel amulet dust.png|thumb|[[Sophie Casterwill]] cries as [[Sabriel]]'s Amulet fades into dust]] While a Titan's spirit is usually immortal and returns safely to its Amulet when a standard battle is lost, there are rare instances where a Titan is permanently lost to its Seeker and its physical form is [[:Category:Destroyed Titans|destroyed]]. Titans can be entirely erased from existence through the use of dark magic or have their physical form permanently lost due to the destruction of their Amulet. In some cases, the spiritual energy of a Titan lives on and is permanently returned to the Spirit World, while in other cases, the Titan ceases to exist entirely. The destruction of an Amulet also causes great discomfort to the Titan's Seeker. {{Source|The Blood Spiral}} {{Source|S2E21}} There are several unique ways for a Titan's physical form or Amulet to be destroyed, rendering them unable to be invoked: *If a Seeker demands that a Titan does not return to its Amulet after taking too much damage, sustaining further consecutive blows will cause its Amulet to permanently disintegrate, destroying the Titan. {{Source|Dante's Return}} Similarly, if a Titan refuses to follow orders or cannot return due to external forces —such as the mental hijacking effect of [[Dominator]]'s spikes— it and its Amulet will be permanently destroyed after taking too many blows. {{Source|The Mission}} *The spell [[Darkvoid]] acts as a black hole that can completely disintegrate anything beyond its event horizon in seconds. In the case of a Titan, it can be pulled in and erased, with their Amulets destroyed for good. {{Source|Memory Lane}} *[[Legion|Legion, the Legendary Titan of War]], can absorb individual Titans and cause their physical Amulets to disintegrate.
